CHAPTER 23 — हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (HRIDAYA-PARIVARTANAM)

Introduction — हृदयपरिवर्तनम् किम्?

The word हृदयपरिवर्तनम् is formed from हृदयम् (the heart) + परिवर्तनम् (change, turning around): हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम् — a 'change of heart'. It names the deepest kind of moral transformation, in which not merely a person's outward behaviour but the inner spring of feeling and intention turns from cruelty to compassion, from selfishness to service. Sanskrit tradition holds that such a change is possible for anyone, however fallen, and that its two great instruments are करुणा (compassion, both received and awakened) and सत्सङ्गः (the company of the good). This lesson tells, in simple original Sanskrit prose, the most celebrated example of a change of heart in Indian tradition — the transformation of the bandit रत्नाकरः into महर्षि वाल्मीकिः, the आदिकवि (first poet) of Sanskrit — and supports the theme with famous public-domain verses on सत्सङ्ग.

कथा — रत्नाकरस्य हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (सरल-संस्कृतेन)

(१) पुरा तमसानद्याः समीपे एकं घोरं वनम् आसीत्। तस्मिन् वने रत्नाकरः नाम दस्युः निवसति स्म। सः मार्गे आगच्छतः पथिकान् अताडयत्, तेषां धनं च अहरत्। तेन धनेन सः स्वस्य कुटुम्बं पालयति स्म। दिने दिने तस्य पापानां राशिः अवर्धत, किन्तु तस्य मनसि पश्चात्तापः न आसीत्।
   शब्दार्थ: दस्युः = robber, bandit; पथिकान् = travellers; अताडयत् = beat, attacked; अहरत् = took away, stole; पालयति स्म = used to maintain; राशिः = heap; पश्चात्तापः = remorse.
   English: Long ago, near the river Tamasa there was a terrible forest. In that forest lived a bandit named Ratnakara. He attacked travellers on the road and took away their wealth, and with that wealth he maintained his family. Day by day the heap of his sins grew, yet there was no remorse in his mind.

(२) एकदा नारदः मुनिः तेन मार्गेण अगच्छत्। रत्नाकरः तं दृष्ट्वा 'तिष्ठ तिष्ठ' इति उक्त्वा तस्य सर्वस्वं ग्रहीतुम् उद्यतः अभवत्। मुनिः भयं विना शान्तः एव अतिष्ठत्। सः करुणया अपृच्छत् — 'भोः! त्वं किमर्थम् एतत् पापं करोषि?' दस्युः अवदत् — 'अहं मम कुटुम्बस्य पोषणाय एतत् करोमि।' मुनिः पुनः अपृच्छत् — 'यस्य कुटुम्बस्य कृते त्वम् एतानि पापानि करोषि, ते सदस्याः तव पापस्य भागं ग्रहीष्यन्ति वा? गृहं गत्वा पृच्छ। अहम् अत्र एव प्रतीक्षां करिष्यामि।'
   शब्दार्थ: सर्वस्वम् = everything one has; उद्यतः = ready, prepared; भयं विना = without fear; करुणया = with compassion; पोषणाय = for the maintenance; भागम् = share; प्रतीक्षाम् = waiting.
   English: Once the sage Narada came along that road. Seeing him, Ratnakara shouted 'Stop! Stop!' and prepared to seize all he had. The sage stood calm, without fear, and asked with compassion, 'Friend, why do you commit this sin?' The bandit said, 'I do this to feed my family.' The sage asked again, 'Those family members for whose sake you commit these sins — will they take a share of your sin? Go home and ask. I shall wait right here.'

(३) रत्नाकरः गृहं गत्वा पत्नीं पुत्रान् पितरौ च अपृच्छत् — 'अहं युष्माकं पोषणाय पापं करोमि। यूयं मम पापस्य भागिनः भविष्यथ वा?' सर्वे अवदन् — 'पोषणं तव कर्तव्यम् अस्ति। पापं तु तव एव। वयं तस्य भागिनः न भवामः।' एतत् उत्तरं श्रुत्वा दस्योः हृदयं कम्पितम्। तस्य नेत्रयोः अश्रूणि आगतानि। सः अचिन्तयत् — 'अहो! येषां कृते अहं पापं करोमि, ते एव मम पापस्य भागं न इच्छन्ति। पापस्य फलं पापकर्ता एव भुङ्क्ते।'
   शब्दार्थ: पितरौ = the two parents; भागिनः = sharers; कर्तव्यम् = duty; कम्पितम् = trembled, was shaken; अश्रूणि = tears; अचिन्तयत् = thought; भुङ्क्ते = experiences, eats (the fruit).
   English: Ratnakara went home and asked his wife, sons and parents: 'I commit sin to feed you. Will you be sharers in my sin?' All of them said: 'To maintain us is your duty; but the sin is yours alone. We shall not share it.' Hearing this answer the bandit's heart was shaken; tears came to his eyes. He thought: 'Alas! The very people for whose sake I sin refuse a share of my sin. The doer alone eats the fruit of his sin.'

(४) सः धावन् नारदस्य समीपम् आगत्य तस्य पादयोः अपतत् — 'भगवन्! मां रक्षतु। मम उद्धारस्य कः उपायः?' करुणापूर्णः मुनिः तस्मै राम-नाम अददात् — 'एतत् नाम एकाग्रचित्तेन जप।' रत्नाकरः एकस्मिन् एव आसने उपविश्य बहूनि वर्षाणि तीव्रं तपः अकरोत्। तपसः कालेन तस्य शरीरस्य उपरि वल्मीकः (an anthill) अभवत्। ततः सः 'वाल्मीकिः' इति नाम्ना प्रसिद्धः अभवत्। एवं दस्युः महर्षिः अभवत् — इदम् एव हृदयपरिवर्तनम्।
   शब्दार्थ: पादयोः अपतत् = fell at the feet; उद्धारः = uplift, deliverance; उपायः = means, way; एकाग्रचित्तेन = with one-pointed mind; जप = repeat, mutter (a name/mantra); वल्मीकः = anthill; प्रसिद्धः = famous.
   English: Running back, he came to Narada and fell at his feet: 'Lord, save me! What is the way of my deliverance?' Full of compassion, the sage gave him the name of Rama: 'Repeat this name with a one-pointed mind.' Sitting in one place, Ratnakara performed intense tapas for many years. In the course of his tapas an anthill (valmika) rose over his body, and from it he became famous by the name 'Valmiki'. Thus a bandit became a maharshi — this indeed is a change of heart.

(५) एकदा महर्षिः वाल्मीकिः तमसायाः तीरे स्नानार्थम् अगच्छत्। तत्र सः वृक्षे क्रौञ्चमिथुनम् अपश्यत्। तौ पक्षिणौ आनन्देन क्रीडतः आस्ताम्। तस्मिन् एव क्षणे एकः निषादः बाणेन तयोः एकं पक्षिणम् अहन्। हतं पतिं दृष्ट्वा क्रौञ्ची करुणं विललाप। तस्याः विलापं श्रुत्वा मुनेः हृदये महती करुणा शोकश्च उत्पन्नौ। शोकाकुलस्य मुनेः मुखात् सहसा छन्दोबद्धा वाणी निर्गता —

   मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः ।
   यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥

   अन्वयः: (हे) निषाद! यत् (त्वं) क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् काममोहितम् एकम् अवधीः, (तस्मात्) त्वं शाश्वतीः समाः प्रतिष्ठां मा अगमः।
   शब्दार्थ: निषाद = O hunter; प्रतिष्ठाम् = standing, repute, peace; मा अगमः = may you not attain; शाश्वतीः समाः = for everlasting years; यत् = because; क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् = from the pair of krauncha birds; एकम् = one; अवधीः = you killed; काममोहितम् = absorbed (deluded) in love.
   English: O hunter, because you killed one of the pair of krauncha birds while it was absorbed in love, may you never attain an abiding place (peace/repute) for everlasting years.
   This grief-born utterance is honoured as the first श्लोक of laukika Sanskrit poetry: मुनेः शोकः एव श्लोकत्वम् आगतः — the sage's grief itself became verse. Soon ब्रह्मा appeared and said: 'By my will this verse came from you. In this very metre (अनुष्टुप्) compose the story of Rama.' Valmiki then composed the रामायणम्, the आदिकाव्यम् (first ornate poem), and is therefore honoured as आदिकविः (the first poet). The same heart that once beat travellers now broke at the death of a bird — the fullest proof of his हृदयपरिवर्तनम्.

सत्सङ्ग-महिमा — supporting verses (with अन्वय and meaning)

(क) भर्तृहरेः नीतिशतकात् —
   जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं
   मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति ।
   चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं
   सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥
   अन्वयः: सत्सङ्गतिः धियः जाड्यं हरति, वाचि सत्यं सिञ्चति, मानोन्नतिं दिशति, पापम् अपाकरोति, चेतः प्रसादयति, दिक्षु कीर्तिं तनोति। कथय, (सा) पुंसां किं न करोति?
   शब्दार्थ: जाड्यम् = dullness; धियः = of the intellect; सिञ्चति = sprinkles, waters; मानोन्नतिम् = rise in honour; अपाकरोति = removes; चेतः = mind; प्रसादयति = makes serene; दिक्षु = in all directions; तनोति = spreads; कीर्तिम् = fame; पुंसाम् = for men.
   English: Good company removes the dullness of the intellect, waters speech with truth, points the way to rising honour, removes sin, makes the mind serene, and spreads fame in every direction. Say — what does the company of the good not do for men? Narada's brief company did exactly this for Ratnakara.

(ख) सुभाषितम् —
   काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गाद् धत्ते मारकतीं द्युतिम् ।
   तथा सत्सन्निधानेन मूर्खो याति प्रवीणताम् ॥
   अन्वयः: काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गात् मारकतीं द्युतिं धत्ते; तथा सत्सन्निधानेन मूर्खः प्रवीणतां याति।
   English: A piece of glass, set beside gold, takes on the lustre of an emerald; so too, by nearness to the good, even a dull person attains proficiency. Contact with the noble transfers nobility.

(ग) शङ्कराचार्यस्य (भजगोविन्दम्) —
   सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वं निस्सङ्गत्वे निर्मोहत्वम् ।
   निर्मोहत्वे निश्चलतत्त्वं निश्चलतत्त्वे जीवन्मुक्तिः ॥
   अन्वयः: सत्सङ्गत्वे (सति) निस्सङ्गत्वं (भवति); निस्सङ्गत्वे निर्मोहत्वम्; निर्मोहत्वे निश्चलतत्त्वम्; निश्चलतत्त्वे जीवन्मुक्तिः।
   English: From the company of the good comes detachment; from detachment, freedom from delusion; from freedom from delusion, steadiness in the truth; and from steadiness in the truth, liberation while yet alive. The ladder of the good life begins on the rung of सत्सङ्ग — exactly where Ratnakara's ascent began.

व्याकरणम् — grammar from the lesson

(A) सन्धिः. Examples drawn from the verses and the story:
   • त्वम् + अगमः → त्वमगमः; पापम् + अपाकरोति → पापमपाकरोति; किम् + अर्थम् → किमर्थम् (म् joins the following vowel).
   • क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् + एकम् → क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम् (त् → द् before a vowel — जश्त्व, व्यञ्जनसन्धिः); एकम् + अवधीः → एकमवधीः.
   • मान + उन्नतिम् → मानोन्नतिम् (अ + उ = ओ, गुणसन्धिः).
   • शोक + आर्तः → शोकार्तः; स्नान + अर्थम् → स्नानार्थम् (अ + आ / अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः).
   • सत् + सङ्गतिः → सत्सङ्गतिः. Splitting a joined form back (e.g. त्वमगमः = त्वम् + अगमः) is सन्धिविच्छेदः.

(B) समासः.
   • हृदयपरिवर्तनम् = हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः).
   • क्रौञ्चमिथुनम् = क्रौञ्चयोः मिथुनम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः).
   • काममोहितम् = कामेन मोहितम् (तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः).
   • महर्षिः = महान् (चासौ) ऋषिः (कर्मधारयः).
   • करुणापूर्णः = करुणया पूर्णः (तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः).

(C) विभक्तिः (case forms in the story): बाणेन 'with an arrow' (तृतीया); कुटुम्बस्य 'of the family' (षष्ठी); वने, तीरे, मार्गे 'in/on' (सप्तमी); मुखात् 'from the mouth' (पञ्चमी); पथिकान् 'the travellers' as object (द्वितीया); मुनेः 'of the sage' (षष्ठी).

(D) लकाराः / कृदन्ताः.
   • लट् (present): करोषि, करोमि, हरति, तनोति। लङ् (past): अगच्छत्, अपश्यत्, अभवत्, अकरोत्, अहन्। लृट् (future): ग्रहीष्यन्ति, भविष्यथ, करिष्यामि। लोट् (command): जप, पृच्छ, रचय।
   • क्त्वा-प्रत्ययः (having done): दृष्ट्वा, श्रुत्वा, गत्वा, उक्त्वा। ल्यप् (with prefix): आगत्य, उपविश्य। तुमुन् (in order to): ग्रहीतुम्। क्त (past participle): हतम्, मोहितम्, कम्पितम्।

SUMMARY (सारांश)

हृदयपरिवर्तनम् — a change of heart — is the turning of the inner person from cruelty to compassion. The lesson's central story shows the bandit Ratnakara, who robbed travellers to feed his family, stopped by the fearless, compassionate question of Narada: 'Will your family share your sin?' When his own family refused, his heart broke open; taking the name of Rama from Narada he performed long tapas, was covered by an anthill (वल्मीक), and rose as महर्षि वाल्मीकिः. His transformed heart proved itself when a hunter killed one of a pair of krauncha birds: his grief burst out as the first श्लोक — मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः... — and, at Brahma's word, he composed the रामायणम्, becoming आदिकविः. Supporting verses — Bhartrhari's जाड्यं धियो हरति..., the काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गात्... subhashita and Shankara's सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वम्... — teach that good company works precisely such change. From the lesson we also drew grammar: सन्धि (त्वमगमः, मानोन्नतिम्, क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम्), समास (हृदयपरिवर्तनम्, काममोहितम्, महर्षिः), common विभक्ति forms, and लकार/कृदन्त forms (अपश्यत्, दृष्ट्वा, आगत्य, ग्रहीतुम्).

topics.name: हृदयपरिवर्तनम् — Meaning and Theme of a Change of Heart
topics.description: The word हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम् = change of heart); inner moral transformation as distinct from outward change; करुणा and सत्सङ्ग as its two great instruments; the chapter's central message that no one is beyond reform.

topics.name: रत्नाकर-वाल्मीकि-कथा — The Transformation of Ratnakara
topics.description: The public-domain legend of the bandit Ratnakara: robbing travellers for his family, Narada's fearless compassionate question, the family's refusal to share his sin, his repentance, Rama-nama and long tapas, the anthill (वल्मीक) and his emergence as महर्षि वाल्मीकिः.

topics.name: मा निषाद — The First Shloka and the Birth of Poetry
topics.description: The krauncha incident on the Tamasa bank; the grief-born verse मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः... with its अन्वय and meaning; शोकः becoming श्लोकः; Brahma's command; the रामायणम् as आदिकाव्यम् and Valmiki as आदिकविः.

topics.name: सत्सङ्ग-महिमा — Verses on Good Company
topics.description: Public-domain verses on the power of good company: Bhartrhari's जाड्यं धियो हरति... (Nitishataka), the काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गात्... subhashita, and Shankara's सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वम्... — each with अन्वय, शब्दार्थ and moral application.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Lesson
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the story and verses: सन्धि and सन्धिविच्छेद (त्वमगमः, मानोन्नतिम्, क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम्), समास with विग्रह (हृदयपरिवर्तनम्, काममोहितम्, महर्षिः), विभक्ति identification, and लकार/कृदन्त forms (लट्-लङ्-लृट्-लोट्; क्त्वा, ल्यप्, तुमुन्, क्त).

topics.name: Translation and Comprehension
topics.description: Word meanings (शब्दार्थ) of key story vocabulary (दस्युः, अश्रूणि, विललाप, मिथुनम्, उद्धारः), translating simple Sanskrit sentences and verses into English, and answering comprehension questions on passages from the lesson.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: हृदयपरिवर्तनम् — Meaning and Theme of a Change of Heart
learning_outcomes.description: Explain the meaning of हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (change of heart) and describe the chapter's central theme that compassion and good company can transform even a hardened sinner.
Recall the events, characters and sequence of the Ratnakara–Valmiki legend, including Narada's counsel, the family's refusal, the tapas and the anthill origin of the name Valmiki.

Analyse the causes and turning points of Ratnakara's transformation — Narada's compassionate questioning, the shock of the family's refusal, repentance and tapas — and the lesson that the doer alone bears his sin.

chapter_summary.title: हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (Hridaya-Parivartanam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary for Chapter 23. It explains the idea of हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (a change of heart), retells the transformation of the bandit Ratnakara into महर्षि वाल्मीकिः, presents the first shloka मा निषाद... with its meaning, studies famous verses on सत्सङ्ग, and draws grammar — सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति and कृदन्त — from the lesson.

branches.label: कथा — Ratnakara to Valmiki
details: Bandit robs travellers for his family
Narada asks: will they share your sin?

branches.label: मा निषाद — First Shloka
details: Hunter kills one bird; the mate laments
Grief becomes verse: शोकः श्लोकत्वम् आगतः

sections.heading: What a change of heart means
bullets: हृदयपरिवर्तनम् = हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम्, the turning of the inner person from cruelty to compassion; deeper than any outward change of behaviour.
Sanskrit tradition holds no one beyond reform — the worst sinner can become a saint when the heart truly turns.
The two great instruments of such change in the lesson are करुणा (compassion) and सत्सङ्गः (the company of the good).

sections.heading: Narada's question and the family's refusal
bullets: The bandit Ratnakara robbed travellers near the Tamasa forest to feed his family, feeling no remorse.
Narada, fearless and compassionate, asked one piercing question: will the family for whom you sin take a share of your sin?
The family answered that maintenance was his duty but the sin was his alone — and this refusal shattered his heart.
Ratnakara realised: पापस्य फलं पापकर्ता एव भुङ्क्ते — the doer alone eats the fruit of his sin.

sections.heading: Tapas and the birth of Valmiki
bullets: Fallen at Narada's feet, Ratnakara received the name of Rama to repeat with one-pointed mind.
He sat in tapas for many years until an anthill (वल्मीकः) covered his body.
From वल्मीक he became famous as वाल्मीकिः — the bandit had become a महर्षि.
The transformation was completed not by punishment but by realisation, repentance and discipline.

sections.heading: The first shloka and the Adikavi
bullets: On the Tamasa bank Valmiki saw a hunter kill one of a loving pair of krauncha birds; the surviving mate's lament filled him with grief.
His grief burst out in metre: मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः । यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥
मुनेः शोकः एव श्लोकत्वम् आगतः — grief itself became verse; this is honoured as the first shloka of Sanskrit poetry.
At Brahma's command Valmiki composed the रामायणम् in the same अनुष्टुप् metre, becoming आदिकविः, and the Ramayana the आदिकाव्यम्.
The heart that once beat travellers now broke for a bird — proof of complete हृदयपरिवर्तनम्.

sections.heading: Satsanga verses and grammar
bullets: Bhartrhari: सत्सङ्गतिः removes dullness of intellect, waters speech with truth, raises honour, removes sin, calms the mind and spreads fame — किं न करोति पुंसाम्?
काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गात्...: glass beside gold shines like emerald; near the good even the dull attain proficiency.
Shankara's ladder: सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वं → निर्मोहत्वम् → निश्चलतत्त्वम् → जीवन्मुक्तिः.

Grammar from the lesson: सन्धि (त्वमगमः, मानोन्नतिम् — गुण; क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम् — जश्त्व), समास (हृदयपरिवर्तनम् षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष; काममोहितम् तृतीया-तत्पुरुष; महर्षिः कर्मधारय), विभक्ति (बाणेन तृतीया, वने सप्तमी, मुखात् पञ्चमी) and कृदन्त (दृष्ट्वा क्त्वा, आगत्य ल्यप्, ग्रहीतुम् तुमुन्, हतम् क्त).

key_takeaways: हृदयपरिवर्तनम् means a change of heart — the inner turning from cruelty to compassion, of which Ratnakara's transformation into Valmiki is the classic example.
One compassionate question from a good person (Narada) can do what no punishment can — awaken conscience.
पापस्य फलं पापकर्ता एव भुङ्क्ते — responsibility for wrongdoing cannot be shared; the doer alone bears its fruit.
Sincere repentance joined to discipline (जप and तपस्) completed the transformation: दस्युः became महर्षिः.
The first shloka of Sanskrit poetry — मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः... — was born from Valmiki's grief for a slain krauncha bird: शोकः श्लोकत्वम् आगतः.
Valmiki is आदिकविः and the रामायणम् is the आदिकाव्यम्, composed at Brahma's command in the अनुष्टुप् metre.
सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् — good company sharpens intellect, truthful speech, honour, purity, serenity and fame; it is the first rung of the ladder to liberation.

glossary.definition: A change of heart (हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम्); the inner moral transformation from cruelty or selfishness to compassion.
A robber or bandit; Ratnakara's occupation before his transformation.
The bandit of the legend who, through Narada's counsel and his own tapas, became the sage Valmiki.
The wandering divine sage whose fearless, compassionate question set Ratnakara's transformation in motion.
An anthill; the mound that covered Ratnakara during his long tapas, from which the name वाल्मीकिः is derived.
A great sage (महान् ऋषिः, कर्मधारय compound); the title Valmiki earned after his transformation.
Austerity, intense spiritual discipline; Ratnakara's years of one-pointed japa and penance.
A pair of krauncha (curlew) birds (क्रौञ्चयोः मिथुनम्); the loving couple of the Tamasa-bank incident.
A hunter; the man who killed one krauncha bird and is addressed in the first shloka as 'मा निषाद'.
A verse; in this lesson, the metre-bound utterance born from Valmiki's शोक (grief) — शोकः श्लोकत्वम् आगतः.
The first poet — Valmiki's title, since the मा निषाद verse is honoured as the first shloka of Sanskrit poetry.
The first ornate poem — the रामायणम्, composed by Valmiki at Brahma's command in the अनुष्टुप् metre.
The company of the good; in Bhartrhari's verse it removes dullness, waters speech with truth, removes sin and spreads fame.
Compassion; Narada's compassion toward the bandit and Valmiki's compassion for the slain bird — the emotion at the heart of the chapter.
Remorse, repentance; the burning regret that turned Ratnakara from sin to tapas.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 23)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give explanations in English. Refer to the story and verses of the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate into simple English:
मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः ।
यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥
questions.answer: O hunter (निषाद), because you killed (अवधीः) one of the pair of krauncha birds (क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् एकम्) while it was absorbed in love (काममोहितम्), may you never attain an abiding place/peace (प्रतिष्ठाम् मा अगमः) for everlasting years (शाश्वतीः समाः).
questions.explanation: This grief-born verse of Valmiki is honoured as the first shloka of Sanskrit poetry.

questions.question: Narrate in 3-4 sentences how the bandit Ratnakara came to be called वाल्मीकिः.
questions.answer: Shaken by his family's refusal to share his sin, Ratnakara fell at Narada's feet and received the name of Rama to repeat. He sat in intense tapas for many years with a one-pointed mind. During this tapas an anthill (वल्मीकः) grew over his body. Emerging from it, he became famous as वाल्मीकिः, the great sage.
questions.explanation: वाल्मीकिः is derived from वल्मीक (anthill), the mound that covered him during tapas.

questions.question: What single question did Narada ask Ratnakara, and why was it so effective?
questions.answer: Narada asked: 'Will the family members for whose sake you commit these sins take a share of your sin?' It was effective because, when his family refused, Ratnakara saw for himself that the doer alone bears the fruit of his sin — a realisation no threat or punishment could have produced.
questions.explanation: The question replaced fear with self-realisation, the true trigger of the change of heart.

questions.question: Do the सन्धिविच्छेद (split) of: (a) त्वमगमः (b) मानोन्नतिम्.
questions.answer: (a) त्वमगमः = त्वम् + अगमः (म् joins the following vowel). (b) मानोन्नतिम् = मान + उन्नतिम् (अ + उ = ओ, गुणसन्धिः).
questions.explanation: Both forms occur in the lesson's verses (मा निषाद... and जाड्यं धियो हरति...).

questions.question: Give the विग्रह and name the समास of: (a) हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (b) काममोहितम्.
questions.answer: (a) हृदयपरिवर्तनम् = हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. (b) काममोहितम् = कामेन मोहितम् — तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः.
questions.explanation: The chapter title itself is a genitive tatpurusha; काममोहितम् from the मा निषाद verse is an instrumental tatpurusha.

questions.question: 'One moment of सत्सङ्ग changed a bandit into the आदिकवि.' Discuss this statement with reference to the story of Ratnakara and Bhartrhari's verse जाड्यं धियो हरति...
questions.answer:
Ratnakara had spent years in sin without remorse, yet a brief meeting with the sage Narada transformed his whole life. Narada did not punish or threaten him; with fearless compassion he asked one question — whether the family for whom Ratnakara sinned would share his sin. The family's refusal shattered the bandit's heart; he repented, received the Rama-nama, performed long tapas under the anthill and rose as महर्षि वाल्मीकिः, who later gave the world its first shloka and the Ramayana.
Bhartrhari's verse explains exactly this power: सत्सङ्गतिः 'removes the dullness of the intellect' (Ratnakara finally understood the law of karma), 'waters speech with truth' (his life turned truthful), 'removes sin' (the bandit's past fell away), 'makes the mind serene' (tapas), and 'spreads fame in all directions' (आदिकविः for all time). The rhetorical question कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् — 'say, what does it not do for men?' — is answered by Ratnakara's life: good company can do everything, even turn a robber into the first poet.
questions.explanation: Connect each benefit listed in the Nitishataka verse to a stage of Ratnakara's transformation.

questions.question: Describe the krauncha incident on the bank of the Tamasa and explain why the verse born from it is called the first श्लोक of Sanskrit poetry.
questions.answer:
One day Maharshi Valmiki went to the Tamasa river to bathe. On a tree he saw a pair of krauncha birds playing joyfully. At that moment a hunter (निषादः) shot the male bird with an arrow; the surviving mate lamented piteously. The sage's heart filled with grief and compassion, and from his mouth burst a metre-bound utterance: मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः । यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥ — 'O hunter, may you never find rest for endless years, for you killed one of this loving pair.'
It is called the first shloka because here, for the first time, spontaneous human emotion (शोकः) took perfect metrical form (श्लोकः) — मुनेः शोकः एव श्लोकत्वम् आगतः. Brahma then appeared and told Valmiki to compose the story of Rama in this same अनुष्टुप् metre. Thus the रामायणम् became the आदिकाव्यम् and Valmiki the आदिकविः, and Sanskrit poetry traces its very birth to a moment of compassion.
questions.explanation: Cover the scene, the verse, शोकः → श्लोकः, Brahma's command, and the titles आदिकवि / आदिकाव्य.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the verse काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गाद् धत्ते मारकतीं द्युतिम् । तथा सत्सन्निधानेन मूर्खो याति प्रवीणताम् ॥ and state its moral.
questions.answer: A piece of glass (काचः), by contact with gold (काञ्चनसंसर्गात्), takes on the lustre of an emerald (मारकतीं द्युतिम्); in the same way, by nearness to the good (सत्सन्निधानेन), even a dull person (मूर्खः) attains proficiency (प्रवीणताम्). Moral: the company we keep transfers its qualities to us — good company ennobles even the ordinary.
questions.explanation: The glass-and-gold image parallels Ratnakara shining after contact with Narada.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: दस्युः, अश्रूणि, विललाप, मिथुनम्, उद्धारः.
questions.answer: दस्युः = robber/bandit; अश्रूणि = tears; विललाप = lamented/wept aloud; मिथुनम् = pair, couple; उद्धारः = uplift, deliverance.
questions.explanation: All five words occur in the story of Ratnakara and the krauncha incident.

questions.question: What does हृदयपरिवर्तनम् mean, and which two forces does the lesson show as its chief instruments?
questions.answer: हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम्) means a change of heart — the inner turning of a person from cruelty and selfishness to compassion and righteousness. The lesson shows its two chief instruments to be करुणा (compassion, like Narada's toward the bandit) and सत्सङ्गः (the company of the good, which awakened Ratnakara's conscience).
questions.explanation: Definition from the compound plus the chapter's two named agents of change.

questions.explanation: हृदयम् (heart) + परिवर्तनम् (change) = change of heart.

questions.explanation: 'Say, what does it not do?' — i.e., it does everything good.

questions.explanation: काञ्चनसंसर्गात् = from contact with gold.

questions.question: In the same verse, by nearness to the good the मूर्खः attains

questions.explanation: निश्चलतत्त्वे जीवन्मुक्तिः — liberation while yet alive.

questions.explanation: It is from the भजगोविन्दम् attributed to Adi Shankaracharya.

questions.explanation: 'Deluded BY love' — instrumental tatpurusha.

questions.explanation: 'Great sage' — adjective + noun, karmadharaya.

questions.question: The विग्रह of 'हृदयपरिवर्तनम्' is
questions.explanation: 'Change OF the heart' — genitive tatpurusha.

questions.question: In 'निषादः बाणेन क्रौञ्चम् अहन्', the word 'बाणेन' is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: बाणेन = 'with an arrow' — instrumental case.

questions.explanation: वने = 'in the forest' — locative case.

questions.question: In 'मुनेः मुखात् श्लोकः निर्गतः', the word 'मुखात्' is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: मुखात् = 'from the mouth' — ablative case.

questions.explanation: अ-augment + past ending: लङ्लकार, past tense.

questions.explanation: -इष्य- marks the simple future, लृट्.

questions.question: 'दृष्ट्वा' (having seen) is formed with which प्रत्यय?
questions.explanation: दृश् + क्त्वा = दृष्ट्वा, 'having seen'.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'दस्युः' means
questions.explanation: दस्यु = bandit, robber.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'विललाप' means
questions.explanation: The krauncha hen lamented (विललाप) for her slain mate.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'अश्रूणि' means
questions.explanation: अश्रु = tear; अश्रूणि = tears (plural).

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'मिथुनम्' means
questions.explanation: मिथुन = pair, as in क्रौञ्चमिथुनम्.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'करुणा' means
questions.explanation: करुणा = compassion, the central emotion of the chapter.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'उद्धारः' means
questions.explanation: Ratnakara asked: मम उद्धारस्य कः उपायः? — what is the way of my deliverance?

questions.question: Translate: 'सः पथिकान् अताडयत्।'
questions.explanation: पथिकान् = travellers (object); अताडयत् = beat/attacked.

questions.question: Translate: 'तस्य नेत्रयोः अश्रूणि आगतानि।'
questions.explanation: नेत्रयोः = in the two eyes; अश्रूणि आगतानि = tears came.

questions.question: Translate: 'निषादः बाणेन क्रौञ्चम् अहन्।'
options: The hunter killed the krauncha bird with an arrow.
The hunter caught the krauncha bird in a net.
The hunter fed the krauncha bird.
The hunter watched the krauncha bird.
questions.answer: The hunter killed the krauncha bird with an arrow.
questions.explanation: बाणेन = with an arrow; अहन् = killed.

questions.question: True or False: हृदयपरिवर्तनम् means a 'change of heart' — an inner moral transformation.
questions.explanation: हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम् = change of the heart, the chapter's theme.

questions.question: True or False: Ratnakara's family agreed to share his sins.
questions.explanation: They refused: पापं तु तव एव — the sin is yours alone.

questions.question: True or False: The word 'वल्मीकः' means an anthill.
questions.explanation: The anthill that covered Ratnakara gave Valmiki his name.

questions.question: True or False: Narada transformed Ratnakara by threatening him with divine punishment.
questions.explanation: He used a compassionate question that led to self-realisation, not threats.

questions.question: True or False: The verse 'मा निषाद...' is addressed to the hunter who killed the krauncha bird.
questions.explanation: निषाद = hunter; the sage's words rebuke him.

questions.question: True or False: The मा निषाद verse is regarded as the LAST shloka of Sanskrit poetry.
questions.explanation: It is honoured as the FIRST shloka; Valmiki is the आदिकवि.

questions.question: True or False: The verse 'जाड्यं धियो हरति...' was composed by Kalidasa.
questions.explanation: It is Bhartrhari's, from the नीतिशतकम्.

questions.question: True or False: According to Bhartrhari, सत्सङ्गतिः removes the dullness of the intellect.
questions.explanation: जाड्यं धियो हरति — it removes the intellect's dullness.

questions.question: True or False: The सन्धिविच्छेद of त्वमगमः is त्वम् + अगमः.
questions.explanation: म् joins the following vowel अ.

questions.question: True or False: 'दृष्ट्वा' is formed with the तुमुन् suffix.
questions.explanation: दृष्ट्वा is a क्त्वा form ('having seen'); ग्रहीतुम् is तुमुन्.

questions.question: रत्नाकरः नाम ____ वने निवसति स्म। (robber)
questions.explanation: A bandit named Ratnakara lived in the forest.

questions.question: तपसः कालेन तस्य शरीरस्य उपरि ____ अभवत्। (anthill)
questions.explanation: An anthill grew over his body during tapas.

questions.question: हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम् इति अस्य समस्तपदं ____ इति। (the chapter title word)
questions.explanation: The compound of हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम् is हृदयपरिवर्तनम्.

questions.question: वाल्मीकिः ____ इति आदिकाव्यं रचितवान्। (the first kavya)
questions.explanation: Valmiki composed the Ramayana, the first ornate poem.

questions.question: मा ____ प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः। (complete the verse)
questions.explanation: मा निषाद — O hunter, may you not attain...

questions.question: यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः ____ ॥ (complete the verse)
questions.explanation: ...for you killed one of the pair while it was absorbed in love.

questions.question: मुनेः ____ एव श्लोकत्वम् आगतः। (the emotion that became verse)
questions.explanation: The sage's grief itself became a shloka.

questions.question: जाड्यं ____ हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यम्। (complete Bhartrhari's line)
questions.explanation: जाड्यं धियो हरति — it removes the intellect's dullness (धियः before ह becomes धियो).

questions.question: सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति ____ ॥ (complete the line)
questions.explanation: ...what does good company not do for men?

questions.question: सत्सङ्गत्वे ____ भवति। (the first fruit in Shankara's chain)
questions.explanation: From good company comes detachment (निस्सङ्गत्वम्).

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत: मान + उन्नतिम् = ____ ।
questions.explanation: अ + उ = ओ (गुणसन्धिः).

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत: त्वम् + अगमः = ____ ।
questions.explanation: म् joins the following vowel: त्वमगमः.

questions.question: 'दृष्ट्वा' इत्यत्र ____ प्रत्ययः अस्ति। (name the suffix)
questions.explanation: दृश् + क्त्वा = दृष्ट्वा, 'having seen'.

questions.question: निषादः ____ क्रौञ्चम् अहन्। (with an arrow — तृतीया form of बाण)
questions.explanation: बाणेन = with an arrow, instrumental case.

questions.question: कुटुम्बस्य उत्तरं श्रुत्वा दस्योः ____ कम्पितम्। (the heart)
questions.explanation: Hearing the family's answer, the bandit's heart trembled.

questions.question: What does हृदयपरिवर्तनम् mean? State the chapter's central message in one sentence.
questions.answer: हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम्) means a change of heart — the inner turning of a person from cruelty and selfishness to compassion and righteousness. The chapter's message is that through compassion and the company of the good, even a hardened sinner like the bandit Ratnakara can be transformed into a saint.
questions.explanation: Definition from the compound plus the theme drawn from the Valmiki legend.

questions.question: What role does सत्सङ्गः play in a change of heart, according to this lesson?
questions.answer: सत्सङ्गः (the company of the good) is shown as the chief trigger of a change of heart. A few minutes of Narada's fearless, compassionate company did what years of ordinary life could not — it awakened Ratnakara's conscience. The lesson's verses confirm this: good company removes dullness, removes sin, and can even lead, step by step, to liberation.
questions.explanation: Connects the story with the जाड्यं धियो हरति and सत्सङ्गत्वे verses.

questions.question: Who was रत्नाकरः and why did he commit robbery?
questions.answer: Ratnakara was a bandit (दस्युः) who lived in the forest near the river Tamasa. He attacked travellers and stole their wealth, and he did this, as he told Narada, to maintain and feed his family (कुटुम्बस्य पोषणाय).
questions.explanation: The story's opening facts: identity, place and motive.

questions.question: How did Ratnakara get the name 'वाल्मीकिः'?
questions.answer: After his repentance, Ratnakara received the Rama-nama from Narada and sat in intense tapas for many years. During this long, motionless tapas an anthill (वल्मीकः) grew over his body. When he emerged from it, he became famous by the name वाल्मीकिः — 'he of the anthill'.
questions.explanation: वाल्मीकिः is derived from वल्मीक (anthill).

questions.question: Describe in 3-4 sentences what happened when Valmiki went to the Tamasa river.
questions.answer: Valmiki went to the Tamasa to bathe and saw on a tree a pair of krauncha birds playing joyfully. At that moment a hunter shot the male bird with an arrow, and the surviving mate lamented piteously. Grief and compassion rose in the sage's heart, and from his mouth burst the metrical verse मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः... Soon after, Brahma appeared and asked him to compose the story of Rama in the same metre.
questions.explanation: The krauncha incident — the birth-scene of the first shloka.

questions.question: What was Narada's question to Ratnakara, and what effect did it have?
questions.answer: Narada asked whether the family members for whose sake Ratnakara committed his sins would take a share of those sins. When Ratnakara asked them and they refused, saying the sin was his alone, his heart was shaken, tears came to his eyes, and he realised that the doer alone bears the fruit of his sin. This realisation turned him to repentance.
questions.explanation: One question replaced years of thoughtless sinning with self-knowledge.

questions.question: Why was the family's reply so significant for Ratnakara's transformation?
questions.answer: His family said that maintaining them was his duty but the sin of robbery was his alone — they would not share it. This showed Ratnakara that the very people for whom he sinned would not stand with him before the law of karma. The prop on which he had justified his sins collapsed, and with it collapsed his old life; the shock opened his heart to change.
questions.explanation: The refusal was the turning point (हृदयं कम्पितम्).

questions.question: 'Narada reformed with a question what a king could not reform with punishment.' Evaluate this statement in the light of the story.
questions.answer: The statement is true to the story's spirit. Punishment works on the body and produces fear, which changes behaviour only outwardly and temporarily. Narada's compassionate question worked on the mind: it made Ratnakara himself discover that no one would share his sin — पापस्य फलं पापकर्ता एव भुङ्क्ते. Because the discovery was his own, the change was inward and permanent: remorse, tapas, and finally sainthood. True reform comes from awakened conscience, not external force.
questions.explanation: Contrast external punishment (fear) with inner realisation (change of heart).

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of the verse मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः । यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥ and translate it.
questions.answer: अन्वयः: (हे) निषाद! यत् (त्वं) क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् काममोहितम् एकम् अवधीः, (तस्मात्) त्वं शाश्वतीः समाः प्रतिष्ठां मा अगमः। Translation: O hunter, because you killed one of the pair of krauncha birds while it was absorbed in love, may you never attain an abiding place (peace/repute) for everlasting years.
questions.explanation: Prose order first, then the sense of each phrase.

questions.question: Explain the saying 'शोकः श्लोकत्वम् आगतः' in the context of this lesson.
questions.answer: When Valmiki saw the krauncha bird killed and heard its mate's lament, grief (शोकः) filled his heart, and that grief burst out of his mouth in a perfectly metrical utterance — the मा निषाद verse. Because raw emotion spontaneously took the form of a metrical verse (श्लोकः), tradition says 'the sage's grief itself became a shloka' — the birth of Sanskrit poetry from compassion.
questions.explanation: The wordplay शोक → श्लोक marks poetry's origin in feeling.

questions.question: Why is Valmiki called आदिकविः and the Ramayana called आदिकाव्यम्?
questions.answer: Because the मा निषाद verse that burst from Valmiki is honoured as the first shloka of (laukika) Sanskrit poetry, Valmiki is called आदिकविः — the first poet. The रामायणम्, which he composed in that same अनुष्टुप् metre at Brahma's command, is therefore the आदिकाव्यम् — the first ornate poem of Sanskrit.
questions.explanation: आदि = first; कवि = poet; काव्य = poem.

questions.question: What did Brahma tell Valmiki after the first shloka was uttered?
questions.answer: Brahma appeared before Valmiki and told him that the verse had come from him by Brahma's own will, and commanded him to compose the story of Rama in that very metre (अनुष्टुप्). Following this command, Valmiki composed the Ramayana.
questions.explanation: Brahma's command turns the single verse into the first epic.

questions.question: Translate Bhartrhari's lines: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति ।
questions.answer: Good company (सत्सङ्गतिः) removes the dullness of the intellect (जाड्यं धियो हरति), waters speech with truth (सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यम्), points the way to rising honour (मानोन्नतिं दिशति), and removes sin (पापम् अपाकरोति).
questions.explanation: Four of the six benefits of satsanga listed in the Nitishataka verse.

questions.question: Explain the simile in काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गाद् धत्ते मारकतीं द्युतिम्... What does it teach about company?
questions.answer: A piece of glass placed in contact with gold takes on the green lustre of an emerald, though it remains glass; similarly, by nearness to the good (सत्सन्निधानेन) even a dull person attains proficiency. The simile teaches that the qualities of our company rub off on us — good company ennobles, so we should choose it deliberately.
questions.explanation: The glass-gold image parallels Ratnakara ennobled by Narada's contact.

questions.question: Explain the step-by-step ladder in Shankara's verse सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वं निस्सङ्गत्वे निर्मोहत्वम्...
questions.answer: The verse builds a four-runged ladder: (1) from सत्सङ्ग (company of the good) comes निस्सङ्गत्व — detachment from bad company and worldly clinging; (2) from detachment comes निर्मोहत्व — freedom from delusion; (3) from freedom from delusion comes निश्चलतत्त्व — steadiness in the unchanging truth; (4) from that steadiness comes जीवन्मुक्ति — liberation while still alive. Each stage causes the next, so the whole spiritual ascent begins with the simple act of keeping good company.
questions.explanation: A causal chain: सत्सङ्ग → निस्सङ्ग → निर्मोह → निश्चलतत्त्व → जीवन्मुक्ति.

questions.question: State any four benefits of सत्सङ्गति listed in Bhartrhari's verse.
questions.answer: Any four of: it removes the dullness of the intellect (जाड्यं धियो हरति); waters speech with truth (सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यम्); points the way to rising honour (मानोन्नतिं दिशति); removes sin (पापम् अपाकरोति); makes the mind serene (चेतः प्रसादयति); spreads fame in all directions (दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिम्).
questions.explanation: Six benefits are listed; any four suffice.

questions.question: Do the सन्धिविच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम् (b) मानोन्नतिम्.
questions.answer: (a) क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम् = क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् + एकम्; त् becomes द् before the vowel — व्यञ्जनसन्धिः (जश्त्वम्). (b) मानोन्नतिम् = मान + उन्नतिम्; अ + उ = ओ — गुणसन्धिः.
questions.explanation: Both forms occur in the lesson's verses.

questions.question: Do the सन्धिविच्छेद of: (a) शोकार्तः (b) पापमपाकरोति, and name the sandhi in (a).
questions.answer: (a) शोकार्तः = शोक + आर्तः; अ + आ = आ — दीर्घसन्धिः. (b) पापमपाकरोति = पापम् + अपाकरोति (the म् simply joins the following vowel अ).
questions.explanation: शोकार्त = 'afflicted by grief', describing the sage.

questions.question: Give the विग्रह and name the समास of: काममोहितम्, महर्षिः, हृदयपरिवर्तनम्.
questions.answer: काममोहितम् = कामेन मोहितम् — तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः (deluded BY love). महर्षिः = महान् ऋषिः — कर्मधारयः (great sage). हृदयपरिवर्तनम् = हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः (change OF the heart).
questions.explanation: Three compounds central to the lesson, with their standard analyses.

questions.question: Identify the लकार (tense/mood) of: अपश्यत्, करोषि, ग्रहीष्यन्ति, जप.
questions.answer: अपश्यत् — लङ् (past: he saw). करोषि — लट् (present: you do). ग्रहीष्यन्ति — लृट् (future: they will take). जप — लोट् (imperative: repeat!).
questions.explanation: All four forms occur in the story.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: पथिकान्, पश्चात्तापः, एकाग्रचित्तेन, प्रतिष्ठाम्, सर्वस्वम्.
questions.answer: पथिकान् = travellers (object form); पश्चात्तापः = remorse, repentance; एकाग्रचित्तेन = with a one-pointed mind; प्रतिष्ठाम् = abiding place, standing, repute; सर्वस्वम् = everything one has, one's all.
questions.explanation: Key vocabulary from the story and the first shloka.

questions.question: Translate into English: (a) मुनिः भयं विना शान्तः एव अतिष्ठत्। (b) सः धावन् नारदस्य पादयोः अपतत्। (c) हतं पतिं दृष्ट्वा क्रौञ्ची करुणं विललाप।
questions.answer: (a) The sage stood calm, without any fear. (b) Running, he fell at Narada's feet. (c) Seeing her slain mate, the krauncha hen lamented piteously.
questions.explanation: Three sentences from different moments of the story.

questions.question: What is हृदयपरिवर्तनम्? Explain the concept with evidence from the chapter, and discuss why the lesson holds that no one is beyond reform.
questions.answer:
हृदयपरिवर्तनम् (हृदयस्य परिवर्तनम्) is a change of heart — a transformation of the inner person, not merely of outward behaviour. The chapter offers the strongest possible evidence: Ratnakara was a hardened bandit who beat travellers and felt no remorse (पश्चात्तापः न आसीत्). Yet one meeting with Narada changed everything. The sage's compassionate question sent him home; his family's refusal to share his sin shattered his self-justification; tears of remorse came; and he surrendered at Narada's feet. Years of japa and tapas under the anthill completed the change, and the bandit rose as महर्षि वाल्मीकिः.
The completeness of the change is proved at the Tamasa: the man who once beat human beings now grieved so deeply for one slain bird that his grief became the first shloka of Sanskrit poetry. The lesson therefore holds that no one is beyond reform: sin is a state of ignorance, not an unchangeable nature. When realisation (ज्ञानम्), remorse (पश्चात्तापः) and discipline (तपः) meet compassion and good company, even the darkest heart can turn — and can turn so far as to give the world the Ramayana.
questions.explanation: Definition, story evidence (before/after contrast), and the doctrine that the heart, once turned, transforms the whole person.

questions.question: Narrate the complete story of Ratnakara's transformation into Maharshi Valmiki in the correct sequence of events.
questions.answer:
1. Ratnakara, a bandit, lived in the forest near the Tamasa, robbing travellers to feed his family, without remorse.
2. One day the sage Narada came along the road; Ratnakara stopped him to seize his belongings, but the sage stood fearless and asked with compassion why he sinned.
3. When Ratnakara said it was for his family, Narada asked him to go home and ask whether they would share his sin, promising to wait.
4. His wife, sons and parents all refused: maintenance was his duty, but the sin was his alone.
5. His heart shaken, in tears, Ratnakara realised that the doer alone eats the fruit of his sin, ran back and fell at Narada's feet asking for deliverance.
6. Narada gave him the name of Rama to repeat with a one-pointed mind; Ratnakara sat in tapas for many years until an anthill (वल्मीकः) covered his body.
7. Emerging, he became famous as वाल्मीकिः; later, at the Tamasa, his grief at the killing of a krauncha bird became the first shloka, and at Brahma's command he composed the रामायणम्, earning the title आदिकविः.
questions.explanation: Seven ordered stages: sin, encounter, question, refusal, repentance, tapas, emergence as sage and poet.

questions.question: Analyse the three factors that together produced Ratnakara's transformation: Narada's compassion, the family's refusal, and tapas. Show what each contributed.
questions.answer:
Narada's compassion opened the door. He stood fearless before an armed robber and, instead of condemning him, asked a gentle question about who would share his sin. Without this करुणा there would have been no occasion for change: fear or force would only have hardened the bandit.
The family's refusal supplied the shock of truth. Ratnakara's whole life rested on the excuse that he sinned for his family. When they said 'the sin is yours alone', that foundation collapsed; the tears and trembling of his heart (हृदयं कम्पितम्) mark the actual moment of the change of heart — realisation that पापस्य फलं पापकर्ता एव भुङ्क्ते.
Tapas completed and stabilised the change. A single moment of remorse can fade; years of one-pointed japa of the Rama-nama burnt away old tendencies and built the new man, until the anthill-covered penitent emerged as महर्षि वाल्मीकिः.
Thus compassion made change possible, truth made it necessary, and discipline made it permanent — all three together, none sufficient alone.
questions.explanation: Each factor mapped to its function: opening, turning, and consolidating the transformation.

questions.question: Quote the first shloka of Sanskrit poetry, give its अन्वय and meaning, and explain its significance for the birth of the Ramayana.
questions.answer:
The verse: मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः । यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥
अन्वयः: (हे) निषाद! यत् (त्वं) क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् काममोहितम् एकम् अवधीः, (तस्मात्) त्वं शाश्वतीः समाः प्रतिष्ठां मा अगमः।
Meaning: O hunter, because you killed one of the pair of krauncha birds while it was absorbed in love, may you never attain an abiding place (peace or repute) for everlasting years.
Significance: The verse burst spontaneously from Valmiki's grief at the Tamasa — मुनेः शोकः एव श्लोकत्वम् आगतः, grief itself became verse — and is honoured as the first shloka of laukika Sanskrit poetry. Brahma then appeared and commanded Valmiki to compose the story of Rama in this very अनुष्टुप् metre. The result was the रामायणम्, the आदिकाव्यम्, and Valmiki became the आदिकविः. Sanskrit poetry thus traces its birth to a moment of compassion for a suffering creature — fitting proof of the sage's transformed heart.
questions.explanation: Verse, prose order, translation, and the शोक→श्लोक→रामायण chain.

questions.question: Explain Bhartrhari's verse जाड्यं धियो हरति... in full, and discuss how a student today can practise सत्सङ्ग in daily life.
questions.answer:
The verse lists six gifts of good company: it removes the dullness of the intellect (जाड्यं धियो हरति); waters speech with truth (सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यम्); points the way to rising honour (मानोन्नतिं दिशति); removes sin (पापम् अपाकरोति); makes the mind serene (चेतः प्रसादयति); and spreads fame in all directions (दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिम्). The closing rhetorical question — सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम्, 'say, what does it not do for men?' — means it does every good thing.
A student can practise सत्सङ्ग by choosing friends who are sincere and hardworking rather than merely entertaining; spending time with teachers and elders of good character; reading noble books, which are the company of great minds; joining study groups and service activities; and limiting the company — including online company — that dulls the mind or normalises wrong conduct. As glass shines beside gold, character grows bright beside the good.
questions.explanation: All six benefits plus concrete modern applications of the principle.

questions.question: Explain, with one lesson example each, the following sandhi processes: (a) दीर्घसन्धिः (b) गुणसन्धिः (c) व्यञ्जनसन्धिः (जश्त्वम्) (d) the joining of म् with a following vowel.
questions.answer:
(a) दीर्घसन्धिः: two like simple vowels merge into one long vowel — शोक + आर्तः = शोकार्तः (अ + आ = आ); likewise स्नान + अर्थम् = स्नानार्थम्.
(b) गुणसन्धिः: अ/आ followed by इ/उ gives ए/ओ — मान + उन्नतिम् = मानोन्नतिम् (अ + उ = ओ), from Bhartrhari's verse.
(c) व्यञ्जनसन्धिः (जश्त्वम्): a final voiceless stop becomes voiced before a vowel or voiced sound — क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् + एकम् = क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम् (त् → द्), from the मा निषाद verse.
(d) म् before a vowel simply joins it as a single word — त्वम् + अगमः = त्वमगमः; पापम् + अपाकरोति = पापमपाकरोति; किम् + अर्थम् = किमर्थम्.
Recognising these joins, and splitting them back (सन्धिविच्छेदः), is essential for reading the lesson's verses correctly.
questions.explanation: Four sandhi processes, each anchored to a form actually occurring in the chapter.

questions.question: From the lesson, explain the four कृदन्त formations क्त्वा, ल्यप्, तुमुन् and क्त, giving two examples of each from the story where possible.
questions.answer:
क्त्वा ('having done', used when the root has no prefix): दृष्ट्वा (having seen — तं दृष्ट्वा), श्रुत्वा (having heard — उत्तरं श्रुत्वा); also गत्वा, उक्त्वा.
ल्यप् (same sense, used when the root has a prefix): आगत्य (having come — समीपम् आगत्य), उपविश्य (having sat down — आसने उपविश्य).
तुमुन् ('in order to', infinitive of purpose): ग्रहीतुम् (in order to seize — सर्वस्वं ग्रहीतुम् उद्यतः); similar forms mean 'to do X'.
क्त (past passive participle, 'done/affected'): हतम् (slain — हतं पतिं दृष्ट्वा), मोहितम् (deluded — काममोहितम्), कम्पितम् (shaken — हृदयं कम्पितम्).
These forms let Sanskrit narrate a chain of actions compactly, as the story of Ratnakara repeatedly shows.
questions.explanation: Each suffix with its rule (prefix vs no prefix; purpose; participle) and story examples.

questions.question: Write five simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) narrating the story of Ratnakara's transformation, and give their English meaning.
questions.answer:
1. रत्नाकरः वने पथिकान् अताडयत्। (Ratnakara used to beat travellers in the forest.)
2. नारदः तं करुणया प्रश्नम् अपृच्छत्। (Narada asked him a question with compassion.)
3. तस्य कुटुम्बं पापस्य भागं न स्वीकृतवत्। (His family did not accept a share of the sin.)
4. सः बहूनि वर्षाणि तपः अकरोत्। (He performed tapas for many years.)
5. दस्युः महर्षिः वाल्मीकिः अभवत्। (The bandit became the great sage Valmiki.)
Together the sentences trace the whole arc: sin, good company, realisation, discipline, transformation.
questions.explanation: Simple लङ्-tense narration using the chapter's own vocabulary.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'मुनिः अपृच्छत् — यस्य कुटुम्बस्य कृते त्वम् एतानि पापानि करोषि, ते सदस्याः तव पापस्य भागं ग्रहीष्यन्ति वा? गृहं गत्वा पृच्छ। अहम् अत्र एव प्रतीक्षां करिष्यामि।'
(a) Who is the मुनिः and whom does he address? (b) What exactly does he ask? (c) Why does he promise to wait?
questions.answer: (a) The मुनिः is Narada, and he addresses the bandit Ratnakara who has stopped him to rob him. (b) He asks whether the family members, for whose sake Ratnakara commits his sins, will take a share of his sin — and tells him to go home and ask them himself. (c) He promises to wait so that Ratnakara can verify the answer personally and return; the realisation must be Ratnakara's own discovery, and the waiting shows Narada's fearlessness and his confidence in the power of the question.
questions.explanation: The passage is the hinge of the story — the question that triggers the change of heart.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'सर्वे अवदन् — पोषणं तव कर्तव्यम् अस्ति। पापं तु तव एव। वयं तस्य भागिनः न भवामः। एतत् उत्तरं श्रुत्वा दस्योः हृदयं कम्पितम्। तस्य नेत्रयोः अश्रूणि आगतानि।'
(a) Who are 'सर्वे' here? (b) What distinction do they draw between पोषणम् and पापम्? (c) What do the trembling heart and tears signify?
questions.answer: (a) 'सर्वे' are Ratnakara's family members — his wife, sons and parents. (b) They distinguish duty from sin: maintaining the family (पोषणम्) is his obligation as its head, but the sin (पापम्) committed in doing so belongs to him alone; responsibility for wrongdoing cannot be transferred or shared. (c) The trembling heart (हृदयं कम्पितम्) and tears (अश्रूणि) signify the collapse of his life-long self-justification and the awakening of conscience and remorse (पश्चात्तापः) — the exact moment of his हृदयपरिवर्तनम्.
questions.explanation: The family's refusal teaches पापस्य फलं पापकर्ता एव भुङ्क्ते.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'करुणापूर्णः मुनिः तस्मै राम-नाम अददात्। रत्नाकरः एकस्मिन् एव आसने उपविश्य बहूनि वर्षाणि तीव्रं तपः अकरोत्। तपसः कालेन तस्य शरीरस्य उपरि वल्मीकः अभवत्। ततः सः वाल्मीकिः इति नाम्ना प्रसिद्धः अभवत्।'
(a) What did the sage give Ratnakara? (b) How did Ratnakara perform tapas? (c) How did he get the name वाल्मीकिः?
questions.answer: (a) The compassionate sage gave him the राम-नाम — the name of Rama — to repeat. (b) Sitting in one single seat (एकस्मिन् एव आसने उपविश्य), he performed intense tapas for many years with a one-pointed mind. (c) During this long tapas an anthill (वल्मीकः) grew over his body; when he emerged from it he became famous by the name वाल्मीकिः, 'he of the anthill'.
questions.explanation: The passage covers the discipline phase that completed the transformation.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'तत्र सः वृक्षे क्रौञ्चमिथुनम् अपश्यत्। तस्मिन् एव क्षणे एकः निषादः बाणेन तयोः एकं पक्षिणम् अहन्। हतं पतिं दृष्ट्वा क्रौञ्ची करुणं विललाप। तस्याः विलापं श्रुत्वा मुनेः हृदये महती करुणा शोकश्च उत्पन्नौ।'
(a) What did the sage see on the tree? (b) What did the निषाद do? (c) Which two emotions arose in the sage's heart, and what did they produce?
questions.answer: (a) The sage saw a pair of krauncha birds (क्रौञ्चमिथुनम्) playing on the tree. (b) At that very moment a hunter (निषादः) killed one of the two birds with an arrow (बाणेन अहन्). (c) Hearing the surviving mate's lament, great compassion (करुणा) and grief (शोकः) arose in the sage's heart; they burst out of his mouth as the metrical verse मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः... — honoured as the first shloka of Sanskrit poetry.
questions.explanation: The krauncha scene, the immediate cause of the first shloka.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः ।
यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम् ॥
(a) Whom does मा निषाद address and what is wished? (b) What reason does the second line give? (c) Why is this verse a rebuke born of compassion rather than a mere curse?
questions.answer: (a) It addresses the hunter (निषाद) and wishes that he may never attain an abiding place, peace or repute (प्रतिष्ठाम् मा अगमः) for everlasting years (शाश्वतीः समाः). (b) The reason: because (यत्) he killed (अवधीः) one bird out of the krauncha pair (क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् एकम्) while it was absorbed in love (काममोहितम्). (c) It is compassion-born because the words spring not from personal hatred but from शोक at innocent suffering — the sage's heart broke for the slain bird and its lamenting mate. Grief for another's pain, taking spontaneous metrical form, is exactly why tradition honours it as the first shloka: poetry born of करुणा.
questions.explanation: Analysis of address, reason clause and the emotional source of the verse.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं
मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति ।
चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं
सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥
(a) What is the subject performing all these actions? (b) List any four actions with their meaning. (c) What is the force of the final question?
questions.answer: (a) The subject is सत्सङ्गतिः — the company of the good. (b) Any four: it removes the dullness of the intellect (जाड्यं धियो हरति); waters speech with truth (सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यम्); points the way to rising honour (मानोन्नतिं दिशति); removes sin (पापम् अपाकरोति); makes the mind serene (चेतः प्रसादयति); spreads fame in all directions (दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिम्). (c) The final rhetorical question — 'say, what does it not do for men?' — asserts that the list is endless: there is no good that satsanga cannot accomplish, as Ratnakara's own transformation proves.
questions.explanation: Bhartrhari's verse analysed as subject + six actions + rhetorical climax.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गाद् धत्ते मारकतीं द्युतिम् ।
तथा सत्सन्निधानेन मूर्खो याति प्रवीणताम् ॥
(a) What happens to glass in contact with gold? (b) What is the parallel stated in the second line? (c) Apply this verse to the story of Ratnakara.
questions.answer: (a) Glass (काचः), set in contact with gold (काञ्चनसंसर्गात्), takes on the lustre of an emerald (मारकतीं द्युतिम् धत्ते). (b) In the same way, by nearness to the good (सत्सन्निधानेन), even a dull or foolish person (मूर्खः) attains proficiency (प्रवीणतां याति). (c) Ratnakara is the glass and Narada the gold: a bandit of no learning, by one contact with a great sage, came to shine with the emerald light of sainthood and poetry — becoming महर्षि and आदिकवि.
questions.explanation: The simile mapped directly onto the chapter's story.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वं निस्सङ्गत्वे निर्मोहत्वम् ।
निर्मोहत्वे निश्चलतत्त्वं निश्चलतत्त्वे जीवन्मुक्तिः ॥
(a) Write the chain of stages in order. (b) To whom is this verse attributed? (c) Show how Ratnakara's life follows this ladder.
questions.answer: (a) The chain: सत्सङ्ग (company of the good) → निस्सङ्गत्व (detachment) → निर्मोहत्व (freedom from delusion) → निश्चलतत्त्व (steadiness in the truth) → जीवन्मुक्ति (liberation while alive). (b) It is attributed to Adi Shankaracharya (from the भजगोविन्दम्). (c) Ratnakara's life climbs exactly this ladder: Narada's company (सत्सङ्ग) detached him from his robber's life and family-excuse (निस्सङ्गत्व); the family's refusal freed him from the delusion that others would share his sin (निर्मोहत्व); years of steady tapas fixed him in the truth (निश्चलतत्त्व); and he emerged a liberated sage, महर्षि वाल्मीकिः (जीवन्मुक्ति).
questions.explanation: The Bhaja-Govindam ladder mapped stage by stage onto the story.

questions.question:
Read the line and answer:
'यत्क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम्'
(a) Do the सन्धिविच्छेद of क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम्. (b) Name the sandhi change involved. (c) Give the विग्रह of काममोहितम् and name its समास.
questions.answer: (a) क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकम् = क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् + एकम्. (b) The final त् of क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् becomes द् before the vowel ए — व्यञ्जनसन्धिः (जश्त्वम्). (c) काममोहितम् = कामेन मोहितम् ('deluded by love') — तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः समासः.
questions.explanation: Grammar analysis applied directly to the first shloka's second line.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer in English:
'सः धावन् नारदस्य समीपम् आगत्य तस्य पादयोः अपतत् — भगवन्! मां रक्षतु। मम उद्धारस्य कः उपायः?'
(a) Translate the narrative sentence. (b) Translate Ratnakara's words. (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of उद्धारः and उपायः.
questions.answer: (a) Running, he came near Narada and fell at his feet. (b) 'Lord! Save me. What is the means of my deliverance?' (c) उद्धारः = uplift, deliverance, rescue (from sin); उपायः = means, method, way.
questions.explanation: Comprehension and translation of the surrender scene.
